title: OceanBench eddy census frame
description: The eddies of one forecast start and lead day (eddy census schema version 4), detected by py-eddy-tracker with the settings of the AVISO META3.2exp NRT atlas. Columnar: element i of every array describes eddy i, whose id is i.

lead_day.description: Lead day of the frame, from 1.

count.description: Number of eddies, the length of every array below.

polarities.description: Names of the polarity codes: anticyclone for a sea level high, cyclone for a sea level low, in both hemispheres.

latitude.description: Eddy-centre latitudes in degrees north, rounded to 3 decimals. Eddies centred less than 5 degrees from the equator are not in the census (parameter minimum_absolute_centre_latitude_degrees of the census metadata).

longitude.description: Eddy-centre longitudes in degrees east, wrapped into [-180, 180) and rounded to 3 decimals.

amplitude.description: Amplitudes in metres: sea level difference between the extremum and the effective contour, on the high-passed field (4 decimals), computed by py-eddy-tracker on the full contour.

effective_radius_km.description: Radius in km of the circle with the area of the full effective (outermost) contour (1 decimal).

speed_radius_km.description: Radius in km of the circle with the area of the contour of maximum mean geostrophic speed (1 decimal).

contour.description: Effective contour of each eddy, simplified (Douglas-Peucker, 0.01 degree tolerance, at most 32 vertices) and without the closing vertex, as an encoded polyline string (the Google polyline algorithm on integers in thousandths of a degree): the successive (latitude, longitude) steps, the first step from the centre. Longitudes are continuous around the centre rather than wrapped, so a contour straddling the dateline overhangs [-180, 180) (e.g. 180.4 next to a centre at 179.8).
